subject.title: Memory compaction blocks main processing lane, causing unresponsive bot for 10+ minutes

question: Should compaction and memoryFlush move to a separate bounded or preemptible maintenance lane, or should OpenClaw keep strict same-session serialization and only shorten/recover the blocking path?
rationale: The code path is clear, but the right behavior affects session ordering, transcript rotation, foreground message delivery, and recovery semantics, so automation should not choose the product contract alone.

options.title: Bounded Maintenance Lane
options.body: Move compaction and memoryFlush out of the foreground session lane with explicit transcript-locking, acknowledgment, timeout, and regression-test coverage.

options.title: Serialized With Recovery
options.body: Keep the current serialization contract but add shorter bounded timeouts, visible busy/error behavior, and watchdog reset so the session cannot remain wedged silently.

options.title: Accept Current Blocking
options.body: Keep the shipped in-band behavior and document timeout/model tuning as the supported mitigation, accepting delayed foreground messages during compaction.

recommendation.title: Bounded Maintenance Lane
recommendation.body: Move compaction and memoryFlush out of the foreground session lane with explicit transcript-locking, acknowledgment, timeout, and regression-test coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The memoryFlush introduction and command-queue serialization history make steipete the strongest available owner for the product contract choice.
